components.input_conditions: The stated full-information causal protocol and at least d^2 rounds.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: d^2 initial rounds yield constant expected regret per coordinate; extra rounds preserve nonnegative expected excess.
components.preserved_model_properties: ||u||=1/8; comparator movement is zero. For any j,y, |w_j-y|<=3/2, grad f=(w_j-y)e_j, Hessian=e_j e_j^T >=(4/9)grad f grad f^T. Thus the losses have gradient bound 3/2 and exp-concavity at least 4/9 uniformly in d.
components.transcript_control: The sequence of other-coordinate labels is independent of a chosen sign experiment. Adaptive decisions add only functions of the available transcript and independent learner randomness, not new samples.
components.transformation: Use d independent scalar biased-sign experiments, each with n=d, theta=1/(8 sqrt(d)); embed conditional means as a fixed point in the radius-1/2 ball.

construction.definition: Let W_d=B_2^d(1/2), theta=1/(8 sqrt(d)). Draw independent uniform signs S_1,...,S_d and fix comparator u_j=theta S_j. In the first d^2 rounds use public deterministic schedule j_t=1+((t-1) mod d), so each coordinate appears d times. Conditional on signs, draw independent labels Y_t in {-1,+1} with mean theta S_{j_t}, and reveal f_t(w)=(w_{j_t}-Y_t)^2/2 after prediction. On any remaining rounds take j_t=1 and continue the same conditional-mean experiment with fresh labels. This explicit schedule instantiates C.3's instruction to query each coordinate d times and continue afterward.
construction.hidden_objects: Independent signs and unrevealed labels; all may be sampled before interaction to form an oblivious distribution.
construction.parameters: d>=1, T>=c0 d^2 with c0>=1; fixed comparator norm ||u||=1/8 and P_T(u)=0; D=1, G<=3/2, eta>=4/9.
construction.public_information: d,T, ball, loss family, bias magnitude, schedule and distribution are public; signs and future labels are hidden. Learner chooses any feasible prediction based on previous revealed functions and independent private randomness.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Scope boundary of the argument; no broader algorithmic easiness claim.
escape_conditions.statement: Disclosure of hidden signs or additional fresh same-sign labels before the prediction invalidates the stated information budget.
This family supplies only the static additive term. Dynamic lower rates need independent block signs and path-budget calibration.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: Every causal proper online learner, deterministic or randomized, with unrestricted computation and full current-loss access after prediction.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No dynamic curved, square-root or saturation branch follows from this static family; those require the distinct block construction C.2.
hardness_claims.regime_note: Only the static additive Omega(d) part, at P_T=0 and T>=c0 d^2.

content.local_transfer_argument: The conditional expected square-loss identity follows by expanding the two squares and substituting E[Y_t|signs,past]=u_j. Sequential_sign applies because each prediction coordinate is in [-1/2,1/2], hence [-1,1], and before its r-th appearance it has only r-1 labels for that sign plus independent other-coordinate information. It yields the quantitative regret bound in information_to_error. Membership follows from the explicit gradient/Hessian calculation in the component. For each fixed randomized learner, average its expected-over-private-randomness regret over the finite sign/label distribution. Since this average is at least 3d/1024 and every generated comparator has zero path length, some deterministic loss-sequence/comparator pair has expected-over-learner regret at least that amount. This establishes the static worst-sequence expected claim without a high-probability assertion.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Indices follow the stated public schedule. Signs are sampled once; labels are conditionally independent given signs. The distribution does not adapt to learner actions.
oracle_realizations.cost: T online rounds, each revealing one whole current loss; not a lower bound on gradient-evaluation counts.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: For each coordinate's first d appearances, d theta^2=1/64<=1/32. Other coordinates' labels and learner randomness are independent auxiliary information for that sign. Full current-function disclosure reveals no other hidden coordinate.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: Conditioned on signs and prior observations, E[f_t(w_t)-f_t(u)]=(w_{t,j_t}-theta S_{j_t})^2/2. Apply sequential_sign to the first d appearances of each coordinate: expected regret per coordinate >=(3/16)d theta^2=3/1024. Sum gives >=3d/1024. Remaining rounds have nonnegative conditional expected excess.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: At each round choose w_t in W_d, then receive the entire function (w_j-Y_t)^2/2, equivalently its public index and single fresh label. Arbitrarily many evaluations of that revealed function reveal no additional hidden-label samples.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: Fresh biased label per round; re-evaluating the same revealed function reuses exactly that label. Learner has no permission to sample future losses before predicting.

use_restrictions: Static-only expected regret hardness; do not claim complete dynamic lower frontier from this family.
Explicit schedule and complete local transfer are submitted for independent checking; no Reviewer result asserted.

links.note: Only its static additive lower contribution, sourced from C.3; this family is not the dynamic construction.

research_use.reason: Each coordinate contributes constant unavoidable cumulative expected error before its fixed small bias can be learned.

summary: A reconstructible zero-movement coordinate-square family forces expected static regret Omega(d); it does not supply dynamic path-dependent branches.
title: Static coordinate-square sign family for additive dimension cost
use_when: Supply the additive dimension initialization cost in full-information exp-concave online regret.
